raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Count real tokens, rather than padding, in packed-schedule FLOPs and TFLOP/s statistics. Each sample is reduced once across DP, without a CP multiplier. Padded execution buffers, and pre-packed samples without real-length metadata, keep their existing behavior.

Rebased after #8592 and removed the dataset-placement fix it already covers. Added DP>1 global-statistics assertions and CPU regression coverage for per-stage scheduling.

Merged main at e1afbb93. Since #8341 moved the dataset-placement predicate into `megatron/training/datasets/providers.py`, the CPU test patches the modules that predicate reads.

## Validation

- CI on ea35d875 (H100): the 9 new CPU cases and all 10 `test_wrap_dataloader` layouts passed on every rank. The run's only test failure was an A2A-overlap NaN on one rank, in a schedule path that main fixed in a0ef646; see the PR comments.
- On 044d6092:
  - 92 CPU tests passed. Negative controls cover padding, DP reduction, placement and the pre-#8341 patch points.
  - An 8-process gloo harness passed all 10 layouts through `wrap_data_iterator` and the `training.py` stats hand-off, with and without the CUDA-graph THD document bound.
  - Lint passed.
- GPU tests for 044d6092 run in CI. No performance run.

No external-source code copied or adapted.

@zhongbozhu Rebased on `main` after #8592; the new head is fae0e53b. #8592's placement rule covers this PR's former placement fix, so I dropped that fix along with its edits to `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py` and `test_get_batch.py`. What remains:

- Real-token FLOPs statistics (`get_global_real_seqlen_stats`), which `main` does not have yet.
- A CPU test that runs the scheduler on every PP stage, including MTP and VPP layouts, with the iterators #8592's placement provides.
- The DP > 1 coverage from the [bot review](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/5993#pullrequestreview-5663842341):
  - `test_wrap_dataloader` now asserts both global values: the rounded-length fallback with no CP factor.
  - It adds the DP = 4, CP = 2 dynamic-CP case.
  - Exact equality happens to hold for this fixture. I still used `pytest.approx`, because TP ranks other than 0 receive the values as float32 through `broadcast_scalars`.

The GPU tests were not run locally. The description lists what was validated on CPU.

CI on fae0e53b ([run 40894709900](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900)) failed in two buckets. Both failures look unrelated to this change.

- **`tests/unit_tests/rl/**`** ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050727)):
  - Testmon selected four files: `test_rl_batch_invariant.py`, `test_rl_utils.py`, `test_rollout_generation.py` and `test_sequence_packing_utils.py`.
  - With that selection, `test_get_logprobs_cuda_graphs[tp2-pp1]` hangs. Rank 1 never reaches the teardown barrier, and all three attempts time out.
  - Runs of four unrelated PRs with the same selection hang the same way ([1](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40898398180/job/123822657148), [2](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40893739076/job/123770139875), [3](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40889005662/job/123822390162), [4](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40886653060/job/123769028405)). [3] is a rerun on a different runner.
  - Selections without `test_rl_batch_invariant.py`, or with `test_context_parallel.py` before it, pass. So does the full directory in the merge group for this PR's base 128d0970 ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40871862403/job/123442428759)).
- **`tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/**`** ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050891)):
  - `test_virtual_expert_planner_graph_replay[dtype0-8]` failed once, with a histogram mismatch after a graph replay.
  - The same test failed as `[dtype0-4]` in a main merge group ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40846742909/job/123357232643)). It passes in other runs with the same selection.

This PR's own tests ran and passed:
- the new `test_packed_schedule_regressions.py` cases ([data job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050661));
- all 10 `test_wrap_dataloader` cases, including DP = 4, CP = 2 ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050887)).

I did not rerun: a rerun reuses the same selection plan, so the RL bucket would hang again.

Updated to main bfab98f4 with a merge commit, followed by ea35d875.

- On current main, the dataset-placement predicate lives in `megatron/training/datasets/providers.py`. It reads `get_args` and the transformer config from `megatron.training.global_vars` and `megatron.training.arguments`, so the per-stage CPU test now patches those modules. With the old patch points it failed with `args is not initialized`.
- The FLOPs change itself is unchanged and still needed, because the scheduler on main sums padded lengths.
- CI for ea35d875: [run 41379122996](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/41379122996). The earlier RL and determinism-kernel failures were not caused by this PR. Main has since changed the local CUDA graph lifecycle (dae43b6), so this run's RL result is new evidence.

CI on ea35d875 ([run 41379122996](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/41379122996)) failed only in the A2A-overlap bucket.

- On rank 4, `test_1f1b_schedule_model_chunk_with_padding_mask[2-layers1-flex-ncclep]` produced a NaN expert `linear_fc1` gradient in the overlap path. The other seven ranks passed every test.
- That test does not reach this PR's code.
- The same symptom appeared in other PRs whose bases predate a0ef646. That commit makes schedule inputs record every consumer stream, and main with it passes the full A2A bucket.

I merged main (e1afbb93), which includes a0ef646, as 044d6092. CI: [run 41603548384](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/41603548384).

+class DpBalancedScheduler(BasePackingScheduler):

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=low -->

The production changes look consistent with the iterator-placement and real-length accounting contracts. One non-blocking regression-coverage gap remains. This was a source-only review; no tests were executed.

### Assert global statistics when DP > 1

The [new regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/tests/unit_tests/data/test_packed_schedule_regressions.py#L667-L680) always supplies a size-one DP group, bypassing the new [statistics reduction](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/megatron/core/datasets/data_schedule_utils.py#L643-L650). Existing distributed coverage either discards the statistics or [checks only their types](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/tests/unit_tests/test_sequence_packing.py#L760-L781). Removing the new reduction would therefore leave the value assertions passing while DP > 1 returns local, rather than global, totals.

**Correction:** extend `test_wrap_dataloader` to assert both global values. Its pre-packed fixture rounds each input length to 16 and carries no original-length metadata, so its expected statistics must retain that fallback—not use the unrounded `nums`. A small proposed addition immediately after its type assertions is:

```python
expected_lengths = [((length + 15) // 16) * 16 for length in nums]
assert num_total_tokens_this_global_batch == float(sum(expected_lengths))
assert sequence_square_sum_this_global_batch == float(
    sum(length * length for length in expected_lengths)
)
```

Also add this case to that test's [parallelism parameter table](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/tests/unit_tests/test_sequence_packing.py#L650-L659), giving the eight-rank suite DP=4 and CP=2 for the inherited dynamic-scheduler path:

```python
(1, 1, 2, None, "default_dynamic_cp"),
```

**Preservation and acceptance:** retain the new unpacked-sample assertions that exclude padding, along with their PP/VPP/MTP field-ownership checks. The distributed pre-packed cases above should equal the rounded-length sums exactly, without a CP multiplier. The existing DP>1 static case and the proposed dynamic case should fail the value assertions if the statistics reduction is removed. These are proposed changes and negative-control checks, not executed results.

*Review generated by codex. This was a full review. Request a full review with `/review reset=true`.*

+def get_global_real_seqlen_stats(batch, dp_group, dev) -> Tuple[float, float]:
+    """Sum the real (unpadded) sub-sample lengths of the global batch and their squares.
+
+    Args:
+        batch: This DP rank's sub-samples as returned by :func:`get_batch_and_global_seqlens`.
+        dp_group: The DP group whose padded lengths were gathered for scheduling.
+        dev: Device for the reduction.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(sum_i L_i, sum_i L_i**2)`` over the real lengths ``L_i`` of every sub-sample in
+        ``dp_group``, as expected by ``num_floating_point_operations``.
+    """
+    seqlens = [sample["original_seq_len"].reshape(-1) for sample in batch]
+    seqlens = (torch.cat(seqlens) if seqlens else torch.zeros(0)).to(
+        device=dev, dtype=torch.float64
+    )
+    stats = torch.stack((seqlens.sum(), seqlens.square().sum()))
+    if dp_group.size() > 1:
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(stats, group=dp_group)
+    seqlen_sum, seqlen_squared_sum = stats.tolist()
+    return seqlen_sum, seqlen_squared_sum
+

+class BasePackingScheduler:
+    """Base class for sequence packing schedulers."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank: int,
+        cp_size: int,
+        dp_size: int,
+        microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage: Optional[int],
+    ):
+        """
+        Args:
+            max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank: The maximum sequence length per DPxCP rank.
+            cp_size: The context parallel size.
+            dp_size: The data parallel size.
+            microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage: The microbatch group size per virtual
+            pipeline stage, only used when enabling VPP, otherwise None.
+        """
+        self.max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank = max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank
+        self.cp_size = cp_size
+        self.dp_size = dp_size
+        self.microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage = microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage
+
+    def get_required_sample_keys(self):
+        """Return the required key of each batch."""
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def get_groups_and_subsamples(self, sample_id_seqlens):
+        """schedule the samples into groups"""
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def run(
+        self,
+        data_iterator,
+        num_microbatches,
+        dp_group,
+        tp_group,
+        pp_group,
+        dp_cp_group,
+        dev,
+        config,
+    ):
+        """
+        Run the scheduler and return the new data_iterator.
+
+        Args:
+            data_iterator: The data iterator.
+            num_microbatches: The number of microbatches to fetch.
+            dp_group: Data parallel process group.
+            tp_group: Tensor parallel process group.
+            pp_group: Pipeline parallel process group.
+            dp_cp_group: Data parallel + context parallel process group.
+            dev: CUDA device.
+            config: Model parallel config.
+
+        Returns:
+            new_data_iterator: The new data iterator (or list for VPP).
+            num_micro_batches: Number of micro batches after scheduling.
+            seqlen_sum_this_global_batch: Total tokens for FLOPs calculation.
+            seqlen_squared_sum_this_global_batch: Sum of squared seqlens for FLOPs.
+        """
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+
+class DpBalancedScheduler(BasePackingScheduler):
+    """Packs sequences in their original order until reaching the max limit of sequence length."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.max_seq_len_all_ranks = self.max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank * self.cp_size
+
+    def get_required_sample_keys(self):
+        """Return the required key of each batch."""
+        return [
+            "tokens",
+            "labels",
+            "loss_mask",
+            "position_ids",
+            "original_seq_len",  # Length of the original sequence length, should be a gpu tensor.
+            "padded_seq_len",  # Length of the padded sequence length, should be a gpu tensor.
+        ]
+
+    def get_groups_and_subsamples(self, sample_id_seqlens):
+        """
+        Packs sequences in their original order until reaching the max limit of sequence length.
+        """
+        sample_id_groups = []
+        packed_id_groups = []
+        sum_seqlen = 0
+        single_microbatch = []
+
+        for i in range(len(sample_id_seqlens)):
+            if sum_seqlen + sample_id_seqlens[i][1] <= self.max_seq_len_all_ranks:
+                single_microbatch.append(i)
+                sum_seqlen += sample_id_seqlens[i][1]
+            else:
+                packed_id_groups.append(single_microbatch)
+                single_microbatch = [i]
+                sum_seqlen = sample_id_seqlens[i][1]
+        if len(single_microbatch) > 0:
+            packed_id_groups.append(single_microbatch)
+
+        # we want the number of packed sequences to be multiple of dp_size
+        # so we move few samples from previous microbatch
+        # to the end of the microbatches if needed
+        num_packed_sequence = len(packed_id_groups)
+
+        # when enabling vpp, we want the number of packed sequences to be
+        # multiple of dp_size * microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage
+        multiple = self.dp_size * (
+            self.microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage
+            if self.microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage is not None
+            else 1
+        )
+        if num_packed_sequence % multiple != 0:
+            remainder = num_packed_sequence % multiple
+            num_to_move = multiple - remainder
+            i = num_packed_sequence - 1
+            while num_to_move > 0:
+                assert i >= 0, "Not enough samples to move"
+                if len(packed_id_groups[i]) > 1:
+                    seq_id = packed_id_groups[i].pop()
+                    packed_id_groups.append([seq_id])
+                    num_to_move -= 1
+                else:
+                    i -= 1
+
+        num_micro_batches = int(len(packed_id_groups) / self.dp_size)
+        for i in range(num_micro_batches):

@zhongbozhu Rebased on `main` after #8592; the new head is fae0e53b. #8592's placement rule covers this PR's former placement fix, so I dropped that fix along with its edits to `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py` and `test_get_batch.py`. What remains:

- Real-token FLOPs statistics (`get_global_real_seqlen_stats`), which `main` does not have yet.
- A CPU test that runs the scheduler on every PP stage, including MTP and VPP layouts, with the iterators #8592's placement provides.
- The DP > 1 coverage from the [bot review](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/5993#pullrequestreview-5663842341):
  - `test_wrap_dataloader` now asserts both global values: the rounded-length fallback with no CP factor.
  - It adds the DP = 4, CP = 2 dynamic-CP case.
  - Exact equality happens to hold for this fixture. I still used `pytest.approx`, because TP ranks other than 0 receive the values as float32 through `broadcast_scalars`.

The GPU tests were not run locally. The description lists what was validated on CPU.

CI on fae0e53b ([run 40894709900](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900)) failed in two buckets. Both failures look unrelated to this change.

- **`tests/unit_tests/rl/**`** ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050727)):
  - Testmon selected four files: `test_rl_batch_invariant.py`, `test_rl_utils.py`, `test_rollout_generation.py` and `test_sequence_packing_utils.py`.

[3] is a rerun on a different runner.

- **`tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/**`** ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050891)):
  - `test_virtual_expert_planner_graph_replay[dtype0-8]` failed once, with a histogram mismatch after a graph replay.
  - The same test failed as `[dtype0-4]` in a main merge group ([job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40846742909/job/123357232643)). It passes in other runs with the same selection.

This PR's own tests ran and passed:
- the new `test_packed_schedule_regressions.py` cases ([data job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40894709900/job/123783050661));

I did not rerun: a rerun reuses the same selection plan, so the RL bucket would hang again.

Updated to main bfab98f4 with a merge commit, followed by ea35d875.

- On current main, the dataset-placement predicate lives in `megatron/training/datasets/providers.py`. It reads `get_args` and the transformer config from `megatron.training.global_vars` and `megatron.training.arguments`, so the per-stage CPU test now patches those modules. With the old patch points it failed with `args is not initialized`.
- The FLOPs change itself is unchanged and still needed, because the scheduler on main sums padded lengths.
- CI for ea35d875: [run 41379122996](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/41379122996). The earlier RL and determinism-kernel failures were not caused by this PR. Main has since changed the local CUDA graph lifecycle (dae43b6), so this run's RL result is new evidence.

The production changes look consistent with the iterator-placement and real-length accounting contracts. One non-blocking regression-coverage gap remains. This was a source-only review; no tests were executed.

### Assert global statistics when DP > 1

The [new regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/tests/unit_tests/data/test_packed_schedule_regressions.py#L667-L680) always supplies a size-one DP group, bypassing the new [statistics reduction](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/megatron/core/datasets/data_schedule_utils.py#L643-L650). Existing distributed coverage either discards the statistics or [checks only their types](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/tests/unit_tests/test_sequence_packing.py#L760-L781). Removing the new reduction would therefore leave the value assertions passing while DP > 1 returns local, rather than global, totals.

**Correction:** extend `test_wrap_dataloader` to assert both global values. Its pre-packed fixture rounds each input length to 16 and carries no original-length metadata, so its expected statistics must retain that fallback—not use the unrounded `nums`. A small proposed addition immediately after its type assertions is:

```python
expected_lengths = [((length + 15) // 16) * 16 for length in nums]
assert num_total_tokens_this_global_batch == float(sum(expected_lengths))
assert sequence_square_sum_this_global_batch == float(
    sum(length * length for length in expected_lengths)
)
```

Also add this case to that test's [parallelism parameter table](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ca94eed167ccf4fd4faee84708e65c1c92474b45/tests/unit_tests/test_sequence_packing.py#L650-L659), giving the eight-rank suite DP=4 and CP=2 for the inherited dynamic-scheduler path:

```python
(1, 1, 2, None, "default_dynamic_cp"),
```

**Preservation and acceptance:** retain the new unpacked-sample assertions that exclude padding, along with their PP/VPP/MTP field-ownership checks. The distributed pre-packed cases above should equal the rounded-length sums exactly, without a CP multiplier. The existing DP>1 static case and the proposed dynamic case should fail the value assertions if the statistics reduction is removed. These are proposed changes and negative-control checks, not executed results.
